question: In JavaScript, why does [10, 9, 1].sort() return [1, 10, 9]?
options: Without a comparator, sort compares the items as text, and "10" comes before "9"
The built-in sort is not stable
sort() only sorts the first two items
Numbers above 9 are not allowed in arrays
explanation: The default sort turns items into strings and compares them character by character. For numbers, pass a comparator: sort((a, b) => a - b).

question: Which input makes insertion sort finish fastest?
options: A list that is already sorted
Every input takes the same time
explanation: On a sorted list, each new item is compared once with its left neighbor and stays put, so the sort takes O(n). Reverse order is the worst case: every item moves all the way left, O(n²).

question: Ana and Ben both scored 90. Ana is before Ben in the original list. You sort by score with a stable sort. Where do they end up?
options: It changes from run to run
explanation: A stable sort keeps items with equal keys in their original order. That is why you can sort by one key and then a second without losing the first order.
